newsitem.title: UK: IBCA cuts Caisse Nationale de Credit Professionel.
newsitem.headline: IBCA cuts Caisse Nationale de Credit Professionel.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Friday it had lowered Belgium's Caisse Nationale de Credit Professionnel (CNCP) short-term rating to A1 from A2.
IBCA also said it had cut CNCP's individual rating to C from B/C.
"The legal rating of 2 remains," IBCA said in a statement.
IBCA said this reflected the uncertainty surrounding the future structure and direction of the CNCP group.

"The agency is maintaning its legal rating due to the state's continued involvement in the ownership -- currently 75 percent -- of the bank and CNCP's role in lending to small and medium-sized businesses in Belgium," IBCA said.
IBCA said CNCP was the central bank to a network of mutual institutions providing credit and guarantee services in Belgium.

"Its management had hoped that the credit unions would acquire most of the bank's capital upon privatisation and that the group would be able to develop a cross guarantee scheme similar to that used by cooperative groups elsewhere in Europe. However, this proved impossible to achieve," the agency said.
"Hence, the privatisation process and the group's structure are likely to take a different form from that envisaged by management and will take some time to finalise," IBCA said.
IBCA said under a Royal Decree recently approved by the Belgian Parliament, various structural changes were being set in motion.
CNCP would change its legal status from a public credit institution to a limited company and its name would be amended to Credit Professionnel, IBCA said.

"Also, CNCP will lose its previous legal supervisory powers for its network of local banks and will be obliged to negotiate service contracts with them. Although a solidarity fund, to which all the local credit unions will be obliged to contribute, is being established, its size has not been finalised," IBCA said.
